user_prompt: What is the effect of iron-fortified condiments or seasonings (for example fortified soy sauce, fish sauce, curry powder, salt or other condiments), compared with the same condiment without added iron, on serum or plasma ferritin concentration in children and adults?  Effect measure: pool as a mean difference (MD) in micrograms per litre (µg/L, equal to ng/mL) using a random-effects model. MD > 0 means higher ferritin with the fortified condiment (favours fortification).  Outcome: serum or plasma ferritin concentration at the end of the intervention, extracted as the mean, SD and number of participants per arm. - Use the end-of-intervention value (mean and SD). If a trial reports only the change in ferritin from baseline (mean change and SD of change), use those for both arms and record that change scores were used. Do not mix an end value in one arm with a change score in the other. - If a trial reports several follow-up times, use the last one. - Convert all values to µg/L (for example pmol/L × 0.445 for ferritin). Record the original unit and any conversion. - If variability is reported as SE or SEM, convert to SD = SE × √n. Check table footnotes for whether "±" is SD or SE. - If ferritin is reported as geometric mean with a confidence interval or on a log scale, use the arithmetic mean and SD where the paper gives them; otherwise record the geometric mean and say so. - Cluster-randomised trials (randomised by village, school, household or family): adjust the sample sizes for clustering by dividing both arms' sample sizes by the design effect, 1 + (average cluster size − 1) × ICC, using the ICC reported in the paper. If no ICC is reported, say so and use the paper's own cluster-adjusted analysis if it has one. - Control: the same condiment without added iron. Exclude trials whose control group received iron supplements or a different fortified food. - Multi-arm trials: include the fortified-condiment arm and the unfortified-condiment arm only. Ignore arms with other interventions (for example iron tablets or nutrition education), or combine fortified arms if more than one. - Include only randomised or cluster-randomised controlled trials of condiment or seasoning fortification with iron (alone or with other micronutrients added equally to both arms).  Do not pool haemoglobin, anaemia prevalence, iron deficiency, soluble transferrin receptor, body iron, growth or adverse effects.
